sam: FYI customer corp-x reporting intermittent 502s and TLS handshake timeouts from their Private VPC to our inference endpoint. Started ~09:05 UTC, affects streaming clients only, sync requests OK.
maria: Which VPC/subnet? Any recent policy changes on their side?
sam: VPC 10.12.5.0/24, they say they recently tightened egress to an allowlist. Logs show repeated TCP SYNs with no SYN-ACK back, then after a few retries it works.
aj: Can you paste a tcpdump snippet or a curl timeout? Also any connection IDs from our side?
sam: tcpdump on customer box (trimmed):
```
09:04:12.123456 IP 10.12.5.23.51192 > 198.51.100.10.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
09:04:12.123789 IP 10.12.5.23.51192 > 198.51.100.10.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460]
# no reply
09:04:12.523000 IP 10.12.5.23.51192 > 198.51.100.10.443: Flags [S]
09:04:13.523000 IP 10.12.5.23.51192 > 198.51.100.10.443: Flags [S]
# then after ~8s connection completes
09:04:20.000000 IP 198.51.100.10.443 > 10.12.5.23.51192: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
```
maria: Interesting — delayed SYN-ACK suggests packets from our side are routed back but dropped earlier in the path, or ephemeral port mapping changed. Do they have a NAT gateway or an on-prem firewall?
sam: They use a managed NAT + perimeter firewall. They've allowed 443 outbound but not a wide ephemeral range. I asked them for their egress rules.
infra-bot: probe run: traceroute to 198.51.100.10 shows last hop at customer FW, TTL expired before NAT stage.
aj: This screams ephemeral port return-path mismatch. If their firewall/NAT rewrites source port outside the allowed return set or blocks high ports, the TCP handshake can be delayed until retransmit picks an allowed port.
infra-eng: Also check NACL ordering — a DENY with lower rule number will trump later ALLOWs and can look like intermittent drops.
maria: Sam — any evidence of NACL denies? We can ask them to run `sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v` or show firewall logs for blocked outbound ports 32768-65535.
sam: Customer replied: their edge FW was configured to allow outbound ports 443 and 80 only, and their NAT appliance was set to map source ports into 61000-62000 range. That mapping wasn't permitted by a NACL rule earlier (deny any -> allow 61000 later). So packets were dropped until kernel retried with different ephemeral.
aj: So two problems: (1) NAT source port pool mapped outside allowed ephemeral range, (2) NACL/SG ordering blocked return path. Fix = widen allowed ephemeral egress ports OR change NAT port pool to fall into allowed ephemeral range, and ensure NACL entries are ordered/numbered correctly.
maria: Quick mitigation for them: update perimeter to allow ephemeral range 49152-65535 (or 1024-65535 if conservative) for TCP, and move any DENY rules after ALLOWs for required subnets. Also ensure security group egress allows high ports back.
sam: They applied a temp rule to allow 49152-65535 outbound on FW and the errors dropped to zero within 2 minutes. Streaming stable now.
aj: Can you capture a post-fix tcpdump to confirm consistent SYN/SYN-ACK RTT?
sam: Post-fix snippet shows immediate SYN-ACK within ms. Good.
infra-eng: For our docs and customer onboarding, we should add a KB: checklist for Private/VPC customers — ensure egress allowlist includes ephemeral ports or NAT port pool aligned, NACL rule ordering note, and avoid restricting source-port ranges on NAT appliances.
maria: I'll draft the KB and add sample iptables/NAT config and suggested NACL entries.
support-bot: Flagging escalation resolved in channel — mark as closed after KB publish.
sam: Assigning follow-ups: @maria write KB, @aj add example CloudFormation NACL rules, @infra-eng confirm with prod networking if we should detect this pattern in our onboarding checks.
aj: Ack, will add a detection probe to our onboarding validation (check for SYN retries pattern from customer-provided tcpdump) and suggest warnings during Private setup.
maria: I'll ping customer with the KB and recommended permanent config change (change NAT pool or open ephemeral egress). closing loop after confirmation.
sam: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
